sections.html:
Craig County is in the northeast corner of Oklahoma, with Kansas to the north and Vinita as the county seat. The 2020 census counted 14,104 residents. Five towns sit within the county: Bluejacket, Big Cabin, Ketchum, Vinita and Welch. A house in any of them is billed by the same county Treasurer, though the city and school levies on the bill differ.

A parcel here may be a town lot, a few acres of pasture or a hay field, and the tax paperwork for each can look quite different. Many homes are older, many parcels are rural, and many owners live elsewhere after inheriting a place from family. Interstate 44 and U.S. Highways 59, 60 and 69 cross the county, and Vinita is about sixty miles from both Tulsa and Joplin, Missouri.

The Treasurer collects the tax, and the County Assessor sets the value it is based on. The Treasurer collects what the Assessor certifies on real estate, personal property and public utilities, then sends the money to the county, towns and school districts under budgets the Excise Board approves. Your bill blends several levies, and the Treasurer does not choose the rate.

The office closes on some days through the year, so call first if you plan to pay in person near a holiday.

Oklahoma law (68 O.S. 2913) sets two payment points: half before January 1 and the rest before April 1. If less than half is paid by December 31, the whole year's levy turns delinquent on January 1. Follow the statewide rule, and call the Treasurer for anything specific to your account.

  • A missing statement does not extend the due date.
  • Back taxes can be marked on a statement, so the printed amount may not be the full balance.
  • A seller who is behind should ask for a written total good through the expected closing date.

Protest first with the Assessor, in writing, within 30 calendar days of the date the valuation notice was mailed. Form 974 from the Oklahoma Tax Commission spells out the process under 68 O.S. 2876.

  1. File Form 974 with the Assessor and state what you believe the market value is.
  2. Back it up with a recent sale, comparable sales or an appraisal.
  3. Attend the informal hearing, which can be held by phone if you ask.
  4. Wait for the Assessor's written decision, due within seven calendar days of the hearing.
  5. If you disagree, appeal to the county board of equalization on Form 976 within 15 calendar days of the decision mailing.

If the Assessor did not change your value from the year before, the form allows a protest up to the first Monday in April. Proceedings must wrap up by May 31 or the board's adjournment date. Miss the 30-day window and the proposed value becomes final for that tax year. Check the date printed on your own notice for the exact deadline.

sections.h2: Unpaid city charges on the tax account
sections.html:
City and town charges such as weed cutting, cleanup, paving and nuisance abatement are sent to the County Treasurer once they are delinquent, and they become a lien on the property account.

This matters most for neglected or vacant houses in Vinita, Welch, Ketchum, Bluejacket and Big Cabin. A title company will see an unpaid mowing bill on the tax account, so ask the Treasurer for a full account printout before you list or accept an offer.

The Treasurer also manages county-owned property acquired at annual sales for delinquent taxes and may sell it with approval from the Board of County Commissioners. If a house you own is far behind, that sale process is the end of the road, so it is worth acting early.

sections.h2: Taxes and paperwork when a house sells
sections.html:
At closing, the title or escrow company asks the Treasurer what is owed and pays it from your proceeds if anything is outstanding.

A cash sale can move fast, since there is no lender underwriting to wait on. A few steps do not go away:

  • Get a payoff or tax certificate from the Treasurer.
  • Clear any special assessment liens.
  • Sign a deed that meets the clerk's formatting rules.
  • Pay documentary stamp tax when the deed is recorded.

The County Clerk keeps the deed records at 210 West Delaware Avenue, Suite 103, Vinita, phone 918-256-2507, open 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM. The online index on okcountyrecords.com goes back to October 1956. Under 68 O.S. 3201, documentary stamp tax is 75 cents for each $500 of consideration, and it applies when the price is above $100.

sections.h2: What Craig County sellers usually run into
sections.html:
Most sellers here deal with age, distance and paperwork.

  • Inherited houses where heirs are spread across several states.
  • Rural lots where the legal description includes acreage and mineral questions.
  • Lake-area properties tied to Grand Lake, which the Pensacola Dam created.
  • Houses with unpaid city charges or back taxes.

Whichever route you pick, start with the Treasurer's balance and the Clerk's records so nothing surprises you in the last week before closing.

faqs.q: Who do I call about property tax in Craig County, Oklahoma?
faqs.a: Call the Craig County Treasurer at 918-256-2286 for bills and payments. The office is at 210 W. Delaware, Suite 104 in Vinita and is open weekdays from 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM. Valuation questions go to the County Assessor at the courthouse.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to protest a Craig County valuation?
faqs.a: You have 30 calendar days from the date the valuation notice was mailed to file a written protest with the Assessor. If your value did not change from last year, the form allows a protest until the first Monday in April.

faqs.q: When do Craig County taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: State law makes the whole levy delinquent on January 1 unless half has been paid before then. The remainder is due before April 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Craig County house with taxes still owed?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is normally paid from your sale proceeds at closing. Ask the Treasurer for a written total and clear any city special assessments that were certified to the county.

faqs.q: What documentary stamp tax applies to a Craig County deed?
faqs.a: Under 68 O.S. 3201 it is 75 cents for each $500 of consideration, and it applies when the price is above $100. It is paid when the deed is recorded with the County Clerk.
